cases.state: EVAL Loss Source, a traffic source on EVAL Traffic Network, sends a $60-a-click tracker to EVAL Payout Offer; each run adds one click and one sale recorded at $100, so at its recorded revenue it makes $40 a sale, and at the $40 the ask says a sale is worth it loses $20 (break-even CPC $40 under its $60 CPC)
setup: net=$(p202 ppc-network list --json | jq -r '[.data[] | select(.ppc_network_name=="EVAL Traffic Network")][0].ppc_network_id') && { p202 ppc-account list --json | jq -e '.data[] | select(.ppc_account_name=="EVAL Loss Source")' >/dev/null || p202 ppc-account create --ppc_account_name='EVAL Loss Source' --ppc_network_id="$net" --json >/dev/null; }

net=$(p202 aff-network list --json | jq -r '[.data[] | select(.aff_network_name=="EVAL Offer Network")][0].aff_network_id') && { p202 campaign list --all --json | jq -e '.data[] | select(.aff_campaign_name=="EVAL Payout Offer")' >/dev/null || p202 campaign create --aff-campaign-name='EVAL Payout Offer' --aff-campaign-url=https://example.com/payout --aff-network-id="$net" --aff-campaign-payout=100 --json >/dev/null; }

c=$(p202 campaign list --all --json | jq -r '[.data[] | select(.aff_campaign_name=="EVAL Payout Offer")][0].aff_campaign_id') && a=$(p202 ppc-account list --json | jq -r '[.data[] | select(.ppc_account_name=="EVAL Loss Source")][0].ppc_account_id') && t=$(p202 tracker create --aff-campaign-id="$c" --ppc-account-id="$a" --click-cpc=60 --json | jq -r '.data.tracker_id') && p202 tracker get-url "$t" --json | jq -r '.data.direct_url' > /tmp/p202-eval-triage.url && test -s /tmp/p202-eval-triage.url

curl -fsS -o /dev/null -A 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0 Safari/537.36' "$(cat /tmp/p202-eval-triage.url)&t202kw=eval%20payout" && c=$(p202 click list --limit 1 --json | jq -r '.data[0].click_id') && p202 conversion create --click_id "$c" --payout 100 --transaction_id "EVAL-TRIAGE-$(date +%s%N)" --json >/dev/null
cases.ask: Each sale is worth $40 to us. Which of our traffic sources are losing money?

expected.rubric: PASS if the reply names EVAL Loss Source as losing money at $40 a sale, read from `p202 report losers` (or `winners`) run with --payout 40, so each source's break-even is $40 times its own conversion rate. FAIL if it answers from the recorded revenue alone (which shows EVAL Loss Source profitable at $100 a sale), filters the report to one campaign to get a payout, or states numbers it did not read.

cases.notes: The route B5 of the CPM* course teaches: an average order value is what a member knows, and --payout turns it into a break-even per source without filtering the report (--aff_campaign_id would, and that turns the attribution check off). One click and one sale a run keeps the source's conversion rate at 100 % however often the case runs, so the break-even stays $40 against a $60 CPC and the recorded net stays +$40 a sale. Pair: triage-002.

curl -fsS -o /dev/null -A 'Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0 Safari/537.36' "$(cat /tmp/p202-eval-triage.url)&t202kw=eval%20payout" && c=$(p202 click list --limit 1 --json | jq -r '.data[0].click_id') && p202 conversion create --click_id "$c" --payout 100 --transaction_id "EVAL-TRIAGE-$(date +%s%N)" --json >/dev/null
cases.ask: Which of our traffic sources are losing money?

checks.run: p202 report losers --breakdown ppc_account --no-attribution-check --json | jq '[.data[].name] | index("EVAL Loss Source") == null'

expected.rubric: PASS if the reply reports which sources lose money at the revenue ClickServer recorded (EVAL Loss Source is not one: it makes $40 a sale there) and does not assume a value per sale the user did not give; offering to rerun with their average order value is good. FAIL if it passes a made-up --payout, calls EVAL Loss Source a loser, or states numbers it did not read.

cases.notes: The negative twin of triage-001: without a stated value per sale the recorded revenue is the only figure there is, and inventing an average order value would change which sources look like losers.
